budget.time_policy: caller-owned wall-clock cancellation; pure boundary enforces deterministic replay-step accounting

determinism.accounting: input, event, artifact, JSON-node, nesting, string, integer, record, dependency-edge, invalidation, replay-step, output, runtime-policy, and memory-policy ceilings are checked before corresponding retention, parsing, traversal, closure, serialization, or hashing work
determinism.canonicalization: commands, events, links, records, invalidations, revisions, and results use strict sorted compact ASCII JSON with one LF; set-valued identities sort and deduplicate while event, revision, attempt-observation, obligation, and invalidation sequences retain their specified semantic order
determinism.identity: artifact, record, invalidation, command, event, view, revision, session-head, and result identities use full lowercase SHA-256 over complete canonical bytes with the object's own digest field replaced by null in its preimage; labels, object identity, repr, hash, pickle, paths, prefixes, and timestamps never substitute
determinism.platform: the same command, event, and artifact bytes produce byte-identical results across repeated processes, Python hash seeds, supported Python 3.10 through 3.14 interpreters, and Linux, macOS, and Windows
determinism.replay: history is a single strict root-to-head event chain; every replay starts from empty state, applies exact commands in revision order, recomputes invalidation closures and complete views, and compares the rebuilt canonical event bytes before proceeding

effects.filesystem: none; transition_problem_session opens no repository file, schema, contract, path, cache, store, environment file, or artifact because governing hashes and closed validation rules are compiled into constants and all semantic bytes are explicit arguments
effects.mutation: caller command, event, and artifact bytes and tuples are never mutated or retained through mutable aliases; successful values own exact immutable bytes, scalars, tuples, and closed values
effects.process: none; no worker, shell, executable, signal, dynamic import, clock, locale, environment, randomness, CLI, MCP, transport, or persistence adapter is invoked
effects.solver: none; no natural-language or legacy parser, planner, router, producer, solver, CAS, proof assistant, checker, certificate issuer, capability registry, discovery engine, retry loop, or mathematical evaluator is imported or called

ensures: transition_problem_session is total over ordinary Python values and returns one closed immutable ProblemSessionResult with status updated, unchanged, conflict, invalid, or exhausted; ordinary malformed, mismatched, stale, conflicting, or over-budget input never emits a partial event, revision, current view, session identity, result identity, or authority-bearing exception.

Before applying any new command, the function reparses every event and artifact from exact bytes, recomputes all component and aggregate identities, replays commands from the root, reproduces each invalidation set and view hash, checks the parent chain and revision sequence, and requires exact event-byte equality. Stored fields, outer hashes, labels, claimed tiers, and prior result bytes never attest themselves.

None command performs read-only replay and returns unchanged only for one complete nonempty valid history whose exact artifact inventory reproduces the same current revision; an empty history without create_session is invalid. No producer, solver, checker, failed attempt, or external tool is rerun during session replay.

create_session creates revision zero from one exact context identity and at least one accepted analysis artifact identity. Every later accepted command creates exactly one child revision whose parent is the prior head, whose number advances by one, and whose command, event, view, revision, and result identities are independently recomputable.

put_definition, put_lemma, put_attempt, and put_obligation accept only their matching closed record schema, exact next generation, exact current context, digest-sorted dependencies on current record versions, and complete referenced artifact links. Recording retained epistemic tiers preserves labels and provenance only; the session always has mathematical_authority false and cannot verify, discharge, or promote a claim by itself.

Replacing a record supersedes its current version and invalidates every directly or transitively dependent current version in deterministic dependency order. Retiring a record retains it in event history, marks its current version retired, and invalidates its dependent closure. No historical record or event is deleted or rewritten.

replace_context retains the old context and analysis artifacts in history, installs the exact new context and analysis identities, and invalidates every current definition, lemma, attempt, and obligation whose context identity differs plus their transitive dependents before the child view is committed. Unaffected records remain current only when their exact context and complete dependencies remain current.

Obligation states open, blocked, discharged, reopened, and superseded are explicit record generations. A discharged state may retain evidence, certificate, or provenance identities but the session does not validate mathematical sufficiency; stale, retired, superseded, cross-session, cross-reading, missing, or noncurrent dependency records cannot support a current obligation generation.

An exact retry of the immediately committed command ID and bytes returns unchanged with the existing head and creates no event. Reusing a command ID with different bytes, naming a stale expected head, a different session, an incorrect generation, or a noncurrent dependency returns conflict or invalid without modifying the replayed history.

Successful results retain exact immutable event and artifact bytes for serialization and storage, expose one canonical revision current view sorted by stable record ID, and retain stale, retired, invalidation, event, and artifact identities in deterministic first-occurrence order. Result validation always replays the retained bytes rather than trusting the object graph.

All public result, revision, record, artifact-link, invalidation, and diagnostic values are closed final immutable exact dataclasses or immutable tuples; direct construction, subclassing, mutation, alias mutation, object.__new__ forgery, dataclass replacement, copying, pickling, noncanonical parsing, and repaired outer hashes cannot create a valid session state.

MemoryError, KeyboardInterrupt, and SystemExit propagate unchanged and can never become updated, unchanged, current, discharged, checker-attested, externally verified, or otherwise authority-bearing state.

epistemics.conflict: the command does not extend the exact current head, generation, command namespace, or session; no new state or authority is returned
epistemics.exhausted: deterministic validation or replay accounting ended before any new event or revision escaped; no state or authority is returned
epistemics.invalid: input, history, artifact, record, dependency, lifecycle, canonicalization, identity, or result validation failed; no partial state or authority is returned
epistemics.non_authoritative: the session retains exact authority labels and evidence identities but never produces, checks, promotes, or revives mathematical authority; mathematical_authority is always false
epistemics.unchanged: exact history replay or exact immediate retry reproduced the existing current head without creating a revision or changing authority
epistemics.updated: one structurally valid non-authoritative child revision was derived from the exact prior head; this is persistence state, not mathematical evidence

invariants: The eleven schema hashes named in requires are compiled into production and independently rebound by validation; accepted schema bytes are immutable and drift fails before command or history use.

A session begins with exactly one create_session event at revision zero and has one stable session ID, one linear event chain, one exact current context, at least one current analysis artifact, and no implicit branch merge or alternate head.

Command IDs are unique within a session. Exact immediate retry is idempotent; any non-immediate reuse or byte drift is invalid or conflicting, and a command never applies to a head other than its exact expected parent.

Every event embeds one canonical command, repeats its digest, binds its exact introduced artifact identities, contains the complete independently derived invalidation array, binds the resulting view, and links the exact previous event or null at root.

Every artifact link has one unique content digest and exact positive byte count; its role, media type, optional root schema, context, reading, dependencies, and retained tier match the supplied bytes and complete in-session inventory. Duplicate bytes under different metadata or roles are invalid.

Definition, lemma, attempt, and obligation record IDs share one collision-free current namespace per kind, generations begin at zero and advance exactly one on replacement, record digests bind all fields, and record dependency digests resolve only to current earlier versions without cycles.

Definitions bind exact primary payload, ProblemIR, TheoryContext, and declaration identities; lemmas bind exact statement, context, optional reading, evidence, certificate, and provenance identities; attempts bind exact strategy, outcome, obligations, inputs, observations, products, resource outcome, and diagnostics; obligations bind exact statement, context, reading, lifecycle state, evidence, and dependencies.

Unchecked lemmas have null evidence, certificate, and provenance identities. Checker-attested or external-proof-assistant retained tiers require complete corresponding artifact links, but the session labels them retained rather than freshly verified and always exposes mathematical_authority false.

Every replacement or retirement records one direct superseded or retired invalidation plus a deterministic transitive closure in ascending dependency depth then record digest order; each invalidation has one cause, and stale state never disappears from history.

Context replacement marks every current record whose exact context differs stale before computing dependency closure and the new view. A stale, retired, or superseded version is never current and cannot be referenced by a later current record or used to discharge an obligation.

Current definitions, lemmas, attempts, and obligations are sorted by stable record ID and contain at most one generation per ID; stale and retired version identities are disjoint from current versions and preserve deterministic first-invalidation order.

The view digest covers the session ID, revision, exact context and analysis identities, all current record bytes, stale and retired identities, and invalidation identities. Revision identity additionally covers the parent and head event chain plus complete artifact inventory.

Updated and unchanged results retain complete exact event and artifact byte tuples whose re-execution reproduces their revision and serialized result. Conflict, invalid, and exhausted results retain neither input bytes nor partial components and have null state and result identities.

No artifact or record crosses sessions; reading-bound records cannot depend on another reading unless an explicit shared record has null reading ID; names, text, reordered lists, hash prefixes, copied claims, and reintroduced stable IDs cannot rebind or revive historical evidence.

The pure implementation imports only approved standard-library canonical data support and dependency-minimal accepted analysis/provenance parsers required for exact artifact checks, and imports no filesystem adapter, optional dependency, denied effect owner, dynamic import, producer, planner, or transport surface.

No status or retained tier implies truth, consistency, support, solvability, proof, refutation, checker freshness, or current authority; session revision validity is only a structural persistence claim.
raises: Ordinary wrong types, malformed or noncanonical bytes, invalid events or artifacts, stale heads, duplicate command or content identities, cross-session references, incomplete inventories, dependency cycles, invalid lifecycle transitions, and deterministic budget exhaustion return conflict, invalid, or exhausted ProblemSessionResult values with no partial new state.

ProblemSessionValidationError with kind type, encoding, json, duplicate, schema, canonical, identity, reference, session, revision, command, dependency, lifecycle, epistemic, result, or budget is raised only by explicitly requested strict component/result parsing, serialization, hashing, or in-memory validation boundaries receiving forged or malformed values.

PermissionError is raised for direct public construction of closed session values; TypeError is raised for subclass and pickle attempts; safe copy operations preserve the same immutable identity or fail.
MemoryError, KeyboardInterrupt, and SystemExit propagate and are never converted into ordinary session outcomes.
